questions.stem:
(a) Describe the air (natural) method of seasoning timber. [5 marks]
(b) State two advantages and two disadvantages of air seasoning. [4 marks]
(c) A timber sample weighs 250 g before drying and 200 g after oven drying. Calculate its moisture content. [3 marks]
(d) State three advantages of the moisture meter method over the oven-dry method. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) timber stacked on firm level foundation off the ground
1 mark: (a) sticks (piling sticks) placed between layers in line for air circulation
1 mark: (a) stack covered with roof against sun and rain
1 mark: (a) ends sealed to prevent end splitting
1 mark: (a) left for months until moisture content falls to equilibrium with air
2 marks: (b) advantages: cheap, little skill/equipment needed (1 each)
2 marks: (b) disadvantages: slow, cannot reach low MC, needs large space, defects possible (any two, 1 each)
3 marks: (c) MC = (250 - 200)/200 x 100 = 25%
3 marks: (d) any three: quick, non-destructive, done on site, portable, many readings (1 each)
questions.explanation: Air seasoning: stack on foundations with sticks, cover, seal ends, wait. Cheap but slow. MC = 50/200 = 25%. Meters are quick, portable and non-destructive.

questions.stem:
(a) Name three framing joints and state one use of each. [6 marks]
(b) Describe the procedure for making a through bridle joint. [6 marks]
(c) State three factors to consider when choosing a joint. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: (a) any three with use: mortise and tenon (table rails), bridle (frames, gates), halving (frames, light frames), mitre (picture frames), dowelled (cabinet frames) (2 each)
1 mark: (b) prepare both pieces to size and mark face sides
1 mark: (b) mark shoulders using try square and knife
1 mark: (b) set mortise gauge to one-third thickness and gauge both pieces
1 mark: (b) saw the cheeks of the tenon member and the slot sides
1 mark: (b) remove waste from slot with coping saw and chisel
1 mark: (b) saw tenon shoulders, test fit, glue and cramp
3 marks: (c) any three: strength required, appearance, type of material, tools available, direction of load, ease of construction (1 each)
questions.explanation: Framing joints: mortise and tenon, bridle, halving, mitre. Bridle: mark shoulders, gauge thirds, saw cheeks, chop slot, fit and glue. Choice depends on strength, appearance, material and tools.

questions.stem:
(a) State four safety precautions when using a wood lathe. [4 marks]
(b) Describe the procedure for turning a cylinder between centres. [7 marks]
(c) Name four turning tools. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) any four: tighten work securely, rotate by hand before switching on, correct speed, tool rest close to work, wear goggles, no loose clothing, remove tool rest before sanding (1 each)
1 mark: (b) prepare square blank, find centres by diagonals
1 mark: (b) mark centres, saw kerf/punch at drive end
1 mark: (b) mount between drive centre and tail centre; tighten
1 mark: (b) set tool rest near and slightly below centre
1 mark: (b) rough to cylinder with roughing gouge at low speed
1 mark: (b) smooth with skew chisel, check diameter with calipers
1 mark: (b) sand and finish while turning, part off
4 marks: (c) any four: roughing gouge, spindle gouge, skew chisel, parting tool, scraper, calipers (1 each)
questions.explanation: Lathe safety: secure work, hand-rotate, right speed, close tool rest, goggles. Turning: centre, mount, set rest, rough, smooth, measure, sand. Tools: gouges, skew, parting tool, scraper.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the stages of applying a varnish finish to a table top. [8 marks]
(b) State four precautions when spraying finishes. [4 marks]
(c) Distinguish between paint and varnish. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) surface preparation: plane/scrape, sand with coarse to fine abrasives along the grain, remove dust
2 marks: (a) fill grain/stain if required, allow to dry
2 marks: (a) apply thin first coat (thinned) with brush along the grain, dry and denib with fine paper
2 marks: (a) apply further coats, denib between coats, final coat left to dry dust-free
4 marks: (b) any four: good ventilation/spray booth, respirator, no naked flames, correct pressure and distance, clean gun after use (1 each)
3 marks: (c) paint is opaque and hides grain; varnish is transparent and shows grain; varnish has no pigment (3 marks for clear distinction)
questions.explanation: Prepare and sand, fill/stain, thin first coat, denib, further coats. Spray safely with ventilation, respirator and no flames. Paint hides grain; varnish shows it.

questions.stem:
A small bookshelf has: 2 sides each 900 x 250 x 20 mm, 3 shelves each 600 x 230 x 20 mm, 1 back of plywood 900 x 640 x 6 mm (finished sizes).
(a) Prepare a cutting list allowing 25 mm on length and 5 mm on width for solid timber parts. [8 marks]
(b) Calculate the total area of plywood needed. [2 marks]
(c) State five items found in a working drawing title block. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) sides: 2 off, 925 x 255 x 20 mm, material named
2 marks: (a) shelves: 3 off, 625 x 235 x 20 mm, material named
2 marks: (a) back: 1 off, plywood 900 x 640 x 6 mm (no allowance or small allowance stated)
2 marks: (a) correct table headings: item, number, length, width, thickness, material
2 marks: (b) area = 0.9 x 0.64 = 0.576 m²
5 marks: (c) any five: title, scale, name, date, projection symbol, drawing number, units (1 each)
questions.explanation: Sides 925 x 255 x 20 (2), shelves 625 x 235 x 20 (3), plywood back 900 x 640 x 6. Plywood area 0.576 m². Title block: title, scale, name, date, projection, number.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a sole proprietorship and a partnership under three headings. [6 marks]
(b) List five business opportunities in woodworking. [5 marks]
(c) State four contents of a business plan. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) ownership: one owner vs two or more partners
2 marks: (a) capital: limited personal capital vs pooled capital
2 marks: (a) decision making/profit: owner alone decides and keeps profit vs shared decisions and profit
5 marks: (b) any five: furniture making, wood turning, upholstery, spray painting, timber merchandising, carving, cabinet making, roofing carpentry (1 each)
4 marks: (c) any four: executive summary, business description, market analysis, operations plan, management, financial plan (1 each)
questions.explanation: Sole traders own, fund and decide alone; partners share. Opportunities: furniture, turning, upholstery, spraying, timber sales. Plan: summary, description, market, operations, management, finance.
